target_hardware.notes: single GPU, no NVLink; PCIe Gen4 host

llamacpp.why_cuda_12_8: bundled CUDA runtime 12.8 runs on any driver advertising CUDA 12.0+; deliberately NOT the 13.4 build because the vast.ai host driver advertises max CUDA 13.2 and PTX JIT from a newer toolkit fails with CUDA_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_PTX_VERSION
llamacpp.verified_on: vast.ai instance <instance-id>, 2026-10-01: CUDA0: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 (24126 MiB, 16843 MiB free)

vllm.status: supported by the harness, NOT verified in this run
vllm.note: required only for the AWQ/GPTQ 4-bit arms of the candidate list; install into /venv/main on the GPU box with `uv pip install vllm==0.30.0` (or pip) and pass --vllm-python /venv/main/bin/python
vllm.wheel_cuda: the default index wheels bundle their own CUDA runtime; sm_86 (Ampere) is comfortably covered

host_assumptions.system_cuda_toolkit: 13.2 (unused by the harness: the llama.cpp CUDA bundle ships its own runtime)
host_assumptions.cpu: AMD Ryzen Threadripper PRO 3975WX (10.67 effective cores on this instance)

metric_definitions.load_time_s: wall time from runtime process start to the server answering /health with 200
metric_definitions.peak_vram_mb: max of nvidia-smi memory.used sampled every 100 ms for the whole session (device-wide, so a co-tenant process inflates it; see baseline_vram_mb)
metric_definitions.prefill_tps: prompt_tokens / ttft_s, computed client-side from the stream
metric_definitions.decode_tps: (completion_tokens - 1) / (t_last_token - t_first_token), computed client-side from the stream
metric_definitions.ttft_s: request sent -> first streamed content token
metric_definitions.agg_tps_cN: total completion tokens over N concurrent requests / wall time of the batch (system throughput)
metric_definitions.per_stream_tps_cN: mean of the per-request decode_tps values inside the batch
